1→# ComfyUI Core Reference
     2→
     3→## Workflow JSON Schema
     4→
     5→A ComfyUI API-format workflow is a JSON object where:
     6→- Top-level keys are string node IDs (usually numeric strings like "3", "12")
     7→- Each node has `class_type` (str) and `inputs` (dict)
     8→- Input values are either literals (int, float, str, bool) or connections
     9→- Connections are 2-element arrays: [source_node_id_str, output_index_int]
    10→
    11→## Type System
    12→
    13→Strict types for node connections:
    14→- MODEL — diffusion model (UNet or DiT)
    15→- CLIP — text encoder
    16→- VAE — variational autoencoder
    17→- CONDITIONING — encoded prompt (NOT raw text)
    18→- LATENT — latent space tensor
    19→- IMAGE — pixel tensor [B,H,W,C] float32 range 0-1
    20→- MASK — single channel [B,H,W]
    21→- STRING, INT, FLOAT, BOOLEAN — primitives
    22→- COMBO — dropdown selection (defined in INPUT_TYPES)
    23→
    24→3D types (used by Hunyuan3D, ComfyUI-3D-Pack, VNCCS, etc.):
    25→- MESH — 3D mesh geometry (vertices, faces, UVs; exportable as GLB/OBJ)
    26→- VOXEL — 3D volume (used for volumetric effects and splat-to-mesh conversion)
    27→- POINT_CLOUD — 3D point cloud (from Gaussian Splatting or NeRF reconstruction)
    28→- TRIPLANE — triplane feature tensor (intermediate 3D representation)
    29→- CAMERA — camera position and rotation data (used by 3D control/viewport nodes)
    30→- POSE — body or hand pose skeleton (used by VNCCS, OpenPose, ControlNet)
    31→
    32→Types must match on connections. IMAGE cannot connect to LATENT input.
    33→3D types follow the same strict matching — MESH cannot connect to IMAGE input.
    34→
    35→## Node Registration
    36→
    37→Custom nodes export from __init__.py:
    38→- NODE_CLASS_MAPPINGS: dict[str, class] — internal name → class
    39→- NODE_DISPLAY_NAME_MAPPINGS: dict[str, str] — internal name → UI name
    40→
    41→Each node class needs:
    42→- INPUT_TYPES (classmethod) → {"required": {...}, "optional": {...}}
    43→- RETURN_TYPES: tuple of type strings
    44→- RETURN_NAMES: tuple of output names
    45→- FUNCTION: str — method name to call
    46→- CATEGORY: str — menu path in UI
    47→
    48→## API Endpoints
    49→
    50→| Method | Path | Purpose |
    51→|--------|------|---------|
    52→| GET | /object_info | All registered nodes with full interface |
    53→| GET | /object_info/{node} | Single node info |
    54→| POST | /prompt | Queue workflow execution |
    55→| GET | /queue | Running + pending items |
    56→| GET | /history | Past executions with outputs |
    57→| GET | /history/{prompt_id} | Specific execution result |
    58→| GET | /system_stats | GPU, VRAM, loaded models |
    59→| GET | /embeddings | Available text embeddings |
    60→| WS | /ws?clientId={id} | Real-time execution progress |
    61→
    62→## Execution Model
    63→
    64→ComfyUI executes workflows by:
    65→1. Topological sort of the node graph
    66→2. Execute each node in dependency order
    67→3. Cache outputs — unchanged nodes skip execution
    68→4. Report progress via WebSocket
    69→
    70→## Common Model Directories
    71→
    72→models/checkpoints/ — full diffusion models (SD, SDXL, Flux, etc.)
    73→models/loras/ — LoRA adapters
    74→models/vae/ — standalone VAE models
    75→models/controlnet/ — ControlNet models
    76→models/clip/ — standalone CLIP models
    77→models/upscale_models/ — upscaler models
    78→models/embeddings/ — textual inversions
    79→models/3d/ — 3D generation models (Hunyuan3D, Meshy, Trellis, etc.)
    80→
    81→## Key Patterns
    82→
    83→- Seed is per-sampler-node, not global
    84→- CONDITIONING must go through CLIPTextEncode (never raw string to sampler)
    85→- Image tensors are [B,H,W,C] NOT [B,C,H,W] (ComfyUI convention)
    86→- ControlNet requires resolution matching with the latent
    87→- Empty latent size must be divisible by 8 (usually 64)
    88→- VAE decode and encode are explicit separate nodes
    89→

1→# 3D Generation Workflows in ComfyUI
     2→
     3→## 3D Data Types
     4→
     5→ComfyUI 3D workflows use these connection types between nodes:
     6→- **MESH** -- 3D mesh geometry (vertices, faces, UVs). Exportable as GLB/OBJ.
     7→- **VOXEL** -- 3D volume data. Used for volumetric effects and splat-to-mesh conversion.
     8→- **POINT_CLOUD** -- 3D point cloud from Gaussian Splatting or NeRF reconstruction.
     9→- **TRIPLANE** -- Triplane feature tensor. Intermediate representation (e.g. Hunyuan3D sampler output).
    10→- **CAMERA** -- Camera position and rotation. Used by viewport and 3D control nodes.
    11→- **POSE** -- Body or hand pose skeleton. Used by VNCCS, OpenPose, ControlNet.
    12→
    13→These follow the same strict type matching as 2D types. MESH cannot connect to IMAGE inputs.
    14→
    15→## Hunyuan3D Pipeline
    16→
    17→Hunyuan3D (Tencent) generates 3D meshes from text or images.
    18→
    19→### Typical Node Chain
    20→1. **LoadImage** or **CLIPTextEncode** -- input conditioning
    21→2. **Hunyuan3DLoader** -- loads the Hunyuan3D model weights
    22→3. **Hunyuan3DConditioner** -- prepares conditioning for 3D generation
    23→4. **Hunyuan3DSampler** -- generates triplane features
    24→5. **Hunyuan3DMeshDecoder** -- decodes triplane to 3D mesh
    25→6. **SaveGLB** or **Preview3D** -- exports the result
    26→
    27→### Key Parameters
    28→- **steps**: 50-100 for quality, 20-30 for speed
    29→- **guidance_scale**: 7.0-10.0 typical
    30→- **resolution**: triplane resolution affects detail (256 = fast, 512 = detailed)
    31→
    32→### VRAM Requirements
    33→- 24GB+ VRAM recommended (RTX 4090 works)
    34→- Reduce triplane resolution to 256 for lower VRAM cards
    35→
    36→## 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)
    37→
    38→Gaussian Splatting creates photorealistic 3D scenes from multi-view images.
    39→
    40→### Common Node Packs
    41→- **ComfyUI-3D-Pack**: comprehensive 3D toolkit
    42→- **ComfyUI-Hunyuan3D**: official Hunyuan3D nodes
    43→
    44→### Output Formats
    45→- `.glb` -- standard 3D interchange, viewable in browsers
    46→- `.ply` -- point cloud format, used by Gaussian Splatting
    47→- `.obj` -- classic mesh format with material support
    48→
    49→## Video-to-3D with Wan2.1
    50→
    51→Wan2.1 (Alibaba) supports video generation that can feed into 3D pipelines.
    52→
    53→### Wan2.1 Variants
    54→- **Wan-T2V**: Text-to-video
    55→- **Wan-I2V**: Image-to-video
    56→- **Wan-Fun**: Creative video effects
    57→
    58→### Integration Pattern
    59→Image -> Wan-I2V (multi-view) -> 3D reconstruction -> Mesh export
    60→
    61→## Model Directory Conventions
    62→- 3D models: `models/3d/` or `models/checkpoints/` (varies by node pack)
    63→- Wan models: `models/diffusion_models/` or `models/checkpoints/`
    64→- Some packs use HuggingFace-style directory downloads (multiple files per model)
    65→
    66→## Splat-to-Mesh Conversion
    67→
    68→Common friction point: converting 3DGS/NeRF output to exportable mesh.
    69→
    70→### Path A: ComfyUI-3D-Pack Marching Cubes (most established)
    71→1. Load splat (Load3DGaussian or equivalent)
    72→2. Marching cubes conversion -- resolution 256 (fast) to 512 (detailed)
    73→3. Optional mesh cleanup
    74→4. GLB export (SaveGLB)
    75→
    76→Pitfalls: low resolution = blocky mesh; GLB may lose UVs; large splats need downsampling.
    77→
    78→### Path B: Trellis2 Native Mesh
    79→Some models output MESH directly -- no conversion needed.
    80→
    81→### Path C: External Bridge
    82→Export splat -> process in Blender/Houdini -> reimport. Best quality when time permits.
    83→
    84→## Viewport & Control Tools
    85→
    86→These are not agent-operated. DISCOVER should surface them when relevant.
    87→
    88→### VNCCS (3D Pose Studio) -- @wildmindai
    89→- Full character posing, lighting, multi-pose, camera control
    90→- Use for: "pose a character", "set up ControlNet lighting"
    91→- Most popular 3D tool in ComfyUI ecosystem (3,126+ likes)
    92→
    93→### Action Director -- @wildmindai
    94→- Interactive 3D viewport, loads FBX/GLB, batch-renders ControlNet passes
    95→- Use for: "camera angle", "render depth map from 3D", "batch ControlNet"
    96→- Complements VNCCS: posing vs. scene/camera control
    97→
    98→### 3DView (Orion NodeFlow) -- @kakachiex
    99→- 3D model viewer inside the ComfyUI node graph
   100→- Use for: "preview 3D model", "view mesh in ComfyUI"
   101→- Prototype stage
   102→
   103→### vewd -- @spiritform
   104→- 3D model loading and display
   105→- Use for: "load 3D model", "import GLB"
   106→
   107→## Tips
   108→- Always check VRAM before loading 3D models -- they're typically larger than 2D
   109→- 3D generation is slower than image generation -- set timeouts to 600s+
   110→- Preview3D nodes may not work in headless mode -- use SaveGLB for exports
   111→- For multi-stage pipelines (image -> 3D), use the pipeline tool to chain stages
   112→

1→# 3D Generation — Partner Nodes & Comparative Guide
     2→
     3→## Partner Nodes (Officially Supported)
     4→
     5→These are maintained by both Comfy-Org and the provider. They follow ComfyUI
     6→coding standards and are less likely to break on updates. Prefer these over
     7→equivalent community alternatives.
     8→
     9→### Hunyuan 3D 3.0 (Tencent)
    10→- Input: text, image, or sketch
    11→- Output: production-quality 3D mesh (GLB)
    12→- Best for: final production assets, detailed structures
    13→- VRAM: 24GB+ recommended
    14→- Strengths: highest quality, multi-input support, texture editing coming
    15→
    16→### Meshy 6 (Meshy)
    17→- Input: text or image
    18→- Output: stylized 3D mesh
    19→- Best for: game-ready stylized assets, fast generation
    20→- Strengths: speed + style consistency, good for game art pipelines
    21→
    22→### Tripo v3.0 (VAST AI Research)
    23→- Input: text or image
    24→- Output: 3D mesh
    25→- Best for: rapid prototyping, quick iterations
    26→- Strengths: fastest generation time, good for exploration
    27→
    28→### Rodin 3D Gen-2 (Deemos)
    29→- Input: text or image
    30→- Output: high-detail 3D mesh
    31→- Best for: realistic/detailed models, architectural assets
    32→- Strengths: highest geometric fidelity
    33→
    34→## Community Alternatives
    35→
    36→### Trellis2 (Open Source)
    37→- Open-source mesh generation
    38→- Best for: experimentation, custom pipelines, research
    39→- Note: may output mesh directly without conversion step
    40→
    41→### ComfyUI-3D-Pack (3,641+ stars)
    42→- Comprehensive 3DGS/NeRF/mesh toolkit
    43→- Best for: splat-to-mesh conversion, NeRF workflows, Gaussian Splatting
    44→- Includes marching cubes, point cloud processing, GLB/PLY/OBJ export
    45→
    46→## Quick Comparison
    47→
    48→When an artist asks "what should I use for 3D generation?":
    49→
    50→| Need | Recommend |
    51→|------|-----------|
    52→| Production-quality assets | Hunyuan 3D (Partner) |
    53→| Game-ready stylized | Meshy (Partner) |
    54→| Quick prototyping | Tripo (Partner) |
    55→| Maximum geometric detail | Rodin (Partner) |
    56→| Open-source / research | Trellis2 (Community) |
    57→| Splat/NeRF conversion | ComfyUI-3D-Pack (Community) |
    58→| Architectural structures | Hunyuan 3D or Rodin |
    59→| Character models | Hunyuan 3D or Meshy |
    60→
    61→## Splat-to-Mesh Conversion Paths
    62→
    63→Common friction point: artists have a 3D Gaussian Splat and need a clean mesh.
    64→
    65→### Path A: ComfyUI-3D-Pack Marching Cubes (most established)
    66→1. Load splat data (Load3DGaussian or equivalent)
    67→2. Marching cubes conversion (adjust resolution for quality vs speed)
    68→3. Optional mesh cleanup
    69→4. GLB/OBJ export (SaveGLB)
    70→
    71→Pitfalls:
    72→- Low marching cubes resolution = blocky mesh (try 256-512)
    73→- GLB export may lose UV coordinates without proper unwrapping
    74→- Large splats may need downsampling before conversion
    75→
    76→### Path B: Trellis2 Native Mesh Output
    77→- Some newer models output mesh directly, no conversion needed
    78→- Check if the generation model already outputs MESH type
    79→
    80→### Path C: External Tool Bridge
    81→- Export splat from ComfyUI
    82→- Process in Blender or Houdini (remesh, UV unwrap, cleanup)
    83→- Reimport cleaned mesh
    84→- Best for highest quality when time permits

   342→    # Check connection type compatibility

   346→        target_class = conn["to_class"]
